Part 1 Project: Juniper Hill Community Garden

The project that closes Part 1 (Sessions 1 to 9): the Plot Board, a small React + TypeScript app for a NEW fictional client, a volunteer-run community garden with twelve plots. A board of the season's plots that people filter by status and by bed, and a form to request a plot. It is built from LOCAL typed data (no API, no server) and uses only Part 1: types, unions and guards (Module 2), components, props, lists, state and events, a form with an action, CSS Modules and accessibility (Module 3). Kicked off in Session 8, checked in and demonstrated in Session 9, handed in a week after Session 9. When Part 1 runs as a course of its own, this hand-in and the Part 1 assessment close the course.

Covers Modules 1–3Kickoff Session 8Check-in Session 9Due 1 week after Session 9Rubric 12 points, complete = no row at 0

Part 1 Project: Scoring Guidance by Row

  1. Types and data. Run npm run typecheck: nothing after the two > lines. Open types.ts: unions, not string; gardener?: string; no any, no as anywhere in src/ (search). Strong = doc comments, and when you add 'archived' to PlotStatus tsc lists statusLabels and statusTones (try it: the written part's W3 shows the output).
  2. Components and props. One file per component with a Props interface; Badge and VisuallyHidden imported, not copied. Strong = callbacks named for events (onStatusChange), no unused props, a PlotFilters component or an equally clear split.
  3. Lists, state and events. Tests D pass (run npm test). Read the board: two useStates, visible computed in the body, key={plot.id}, aria-expanded on the toggle. A stored count or list keeps the row at 0 until fixed. Strong = select values narrowed with guards.
  4. A form with actions. Tests E pass. Read RequestForm: useActionState, a state union (editing / sent), validateRequest pure, FieldError under every field with aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Strong = submit it with mistakes in the browser: what was typed stays (defaultValue, the select's key).
  5. Styling and accessibility. npm run lint: 0 warnings and 0 errors (jsx-a11y on). Search src/ for className=": nothing. A two-minute keyboard pass: the ring is visible everywhere (Marigold in the header, green on the page), the card buttons say Show details for Plot N. Strong = a 390 px check and dark mode noted in the journal.
  6. Checks and explanation. The four commands pass on npm ci. From the demo and the journal: one plot from the data to its card, one request to the status line, one decision with its alternative. Strong = the trade-off has a condition ("a switch when the cases do work; a Record when they are data").

Part 1 Project: Model Solution

The model meets every row and reaches "strong" on rows 1, 3 and 4; it leaves the stretch items (a third filter, a summary per bed, a declaration file) to learners. src/types.ts:

// Juniper Hill Community Garden: the plot board's data, described once (TODO A)

/** Where a plot is: a raised bed, a plot in the ground, or a bench in the greenhouse */
export type BedKind = 'raised' | 'ground' | 'greenhouse'

/** open = anyone can request it; assigned = a gardener has it this season; resting = left fallow this season */
export type PlotStatus = 'open' | 'assigned' | 'resting'

export interface Plot {
  id: string
  number: number
  bed: BedKind
  sizeSqFt: number
  sunHours: number
  status: PlotStatus
  /** Only assigned plots have a gardener */
  gardener?: string
  notes: string
}

/** What a valid request holds once the form's text has been checked */
export interface PlotRequest {
  name: string
  email: string
  bed: BedKind
  householdSize: number
}

src/components/PlotBoard.tsx, the derived list and count:

import { useState } from 'react'
import { plots } from '../data/plots.ts'
import { countLine, filterPlots, type BedFilter, type StatusFilter } from '../utils/labels.ts'
import styles from './PlotBoard.module.css'
import { PlotCard } from './PlotCard.tsx'
import { PlotFilters } from './PlotFilters.tsx'

export function PlotBoard() {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<StatusFilter>('all')
  const [bed, setBed] = useState<BedFilter>('all')

  // Derived on every render, never stored: the list and its count always agree with the filters
  const visible = filterPlots(plots, status, bed)

  function clearFilters() {
    setStatus('all')
    setBed('all')
  }

  return (
    <>
      <PlotFilters
        status={status}
        bed={bed}
        onStatusChange={setStatus}
        onBedChange={setBed}
        onClear={clearFilters}
      />
      <p className={styles.count} role="status">
        {countLine(visible.length, plots.length)}
      </p>
      {visible.length === 0 ? (
        <p className={styles.empty}>No plots match these filters.</p>
      ) : (
        <ul className={styles.list}>
          {visible.map((plot) => (
            <li key={plot.id}>
              <PlotCard plot={plot} />
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </>
  )
}

src/components/RequestForm.tsx, the form's action and its state (the fields follow Lesson 3.5's fieldProps pattern):

import { useActionState } from 'react'
import type { PlotRequest } from '../types.ts'
import { bedKinds, bedLabels, isBedKind } from '../utils/labels.ts'
import {
  emptyValues,
  readValues,
  validateRequest,
  type FieldErrors,
  type RequestField,
  type RequestValues,
} from '../utils/requestForm.ts'
import buttonStyles from './Button.module.css'
import { FieldError } from './FieldError.tsx'
import formStyles from './Form.module.css'

// What the form shows: what the person typed and what to fix, or the request it received
type FormState =
  | { kind: 'editing'; values: RequestValues; errors: FieldErrors }
  | { kind: 'sent'; request: PlotRequest }

const initialState: FormState = { kind: 'editing', values: emptyValues, errors: {} }

// The form's action: React calls it with the previous state and the submitted FormData
function sendRequest(_previous: FormState, formData: FormData): FormState {
  const values = readValues(formData)
  const errors = validateRequest(values)
  // isBedKind narrows the text to a BedKind (validateRequest has already said it is one)
  if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0 || !isBedKind(values.bed)) {
    return { kind: 'editing', values, errors }
  }
  return {
    kind: 'sent',
    request: {
      name: values.name,
      email: values.email,
      bed: values.bed,
      householdSize: Number(values.householdSize),
    },
  }
}

export function RequestForm() {
  const [state, formAction] = useActionState(sendRequest, initialState)
  const values = state.kind === 'editing' ? state.values : emptyValues
  const errors = state.kind === 'editing' ? state.errors : {}

  // The props every field needs: its name, a link to its message, and whether it is invalid
  function fieldProps(field: RequestField) {
    const invalid = errors[field] !== undefined
    return {
      id: field,
      name: field,
      'aria-invalid': invalid,
      'aria-describedby': invalid ? `${field}-error` : undefined,
    }
  }
  // ... the fields, each with its label, defaultValue and FieldError (see solution/)
}

Part 1 Project: Instructor Notes

  • Sizing. The kickoff (65 minutes in Session 8) gets everyone through setup and TODO A, and most through TODO B. The rest is three to four hours at home before the Session 9 check-in, plus polish before the hand-in a week later. TODO E is Lesson 3.5's project with other names: learners who finished that lesson move fastest there.
  • Why local data. Part 1 ends before fetching (Lesson 4.1). Everything runs offline: npm install once, then no network and no API. Learners who know fetch already may not add it: the rubric scores what Part 1 teaches.
  • Where it lives. A folder next to the course app (shoreline/juniper-hill/), never inside shoreline-hq/. It has its own package.json, its own tests and its own dev server: two dev servers at once get two ports (Vite prints the second one).
  • The @ts-expect-error test (TODO A). While PlotStatus is still string, tsc reports TS2578 Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive in the test file: the test passes only when the union is exact. Explain it once in the kickoff; otherwise learners edit the test file.
  • The space in the button name (TODO C). Browsers name the button Show details for Plot 3 either way; jsdom (Testing Library) drops a space that sits at the start of the hidden text. Show details{' '}<VisuallyHidden>for Plot 3</VisuallyHidden> works in both, and Shoreline Crew HQ's tests in Module 9 use the same form.
  • A harmless warning. jsdom prints The tag <search> is unrecognized in this browser when a test renders the filters: the course app uses <search> too (Lesson 3.4), browsers support it, the tests still pass.
  • Most common problems, and the nudge. gardener not optional (tsc on plots.ts: "Property 'gardener' is missing"); the visible list or the count in useState (ask: can you work it out from the filters?); a select whose onChange passes event.target.value straight into state (TS2345: narrow it with isBedKind / a status guard); keys from the index; the form's messages in an alert() or the console; className="card" strings left after styling (search for className="); the checkbox's FormData value is null when it is not ticked (that is why readText returns '').
  • Scoring. Run the four commands yourself on the hand-in (npm ci first). Then a two-minute keyboard pass (Tab through the filters, a card's button, the form; submit it empty) and a look at 390 px. Score each row from the evidence; write one sentence per row that is not "strong".
  • Pairs. Allowed if both can explain every line in the demo; score each learner's row 6 separately.
  • Resubmission. A row at 0 gets a written next step and one resubmission within two weeks. The Part 1 result is recorded when both the project and the assessment are met.

Part 1 Assessment

Taken in Session 9 after the project check-in: a written part (15 minutes, closed book, 10 points) and a practical (30 minutes, open book: lesson pages, own code, MDN; no chat assistants, no classmates; 10 points). Total 20; 14 or more (70 %) = the Part 1 assessment met. Learners write the written part in Session 9's workbook; the practical is labs/module-09/part1-practical/ (installed at home beforehand).

Written part: questions, model answers, marking
W1
A teammate runs node plots.ts on a file that has a type error, and Node prints a result. Why does Node not complain, and which command finds the error? (1)
Node removes the types and runs the JavaScript that is left: it never checks them. npx tsc --noEmit (here npm run typecheck, or npm run build, which runs tsc first) reads the types and reports the error.
Marking: The point needs both halves: running is not checking, and a tsc command.
W2
A learner shows the gardener's name in capitals and tsc prints the error below. What does it mean, and how do you fix it? (2)
src/components/PlotCard.tsx:26:77 - error TS18048: 'plot.gardener' is possibly 'undefined'.
Found 1 error in src/components/PlotCard.tsx:26
gardener is optional in Plot (gardener?: string), so its type is string | undefined, and checking plot.status === 'assigned' does not tell TypeScript that the name is there. Fix: check the property itself, plot.gardener !== undefined && ... (or plot.gardener?.toUpperCase()).
Marking: 1 point for "possibly undefined because it is optional", 1 for a fix that narrows. A non-null assertion ! or as string scores 0 for the fix.
W3
The garden adds a fourth status, 'archived', to PlotStatus. What does npm run typecheck do next, and why is that useful? (1)
It reports every Record<PlotStatus, ...> table that has no entry for 'archived' (here statusLabels and statusTones in labels.ts, TS2741). The compiler lists every place the new status needs a decision, before anything runs.
src/utils/labels.ts:12:14 - error TS2741: Property 'archived' is missing in type '{ open: string; assigned: string; resting: string; }' but required in type 'Record<PlotStatus, string>'.
src/utils/labels.ts:18:14 - error TS2741: Property 'archived' is missing in type '{ open: "success"; assigned: "info"; resting: "neutral"; }' but required in type 'Record<PlotStatus, BadgeTone>'.
Found 2 errors in the same file, starting at: src/utils/labels.ts:12
Marking: The point needs "it lists the tables missing the new key".
W4
Why does the plot list use key={plot.id} and not the array index? (1)
A key tells React which item is which between renders. When the filters remove or reorder plots, an index key would point at a different plot, so state such as an open details toggle would jump to the wrong card. An id stays with its plot.
Marking: Accept any answer that ties the key to the item's identity when the list changes.
W5
A board keeps const [shown, setShown] = useState(0) and updates it in useEffect(() => setShown(visible.length), [visible]). What is wrong, and what do you write instead? (2)
The count can be worked out from state on every render: storing it adds a second render and a moment where the number and the list disagree (and visible is a new array each render, so the effect runs every time). Write const shown = visible.length (derived, never stored).
Marking: 1 point for "derived value kept in state", 1 for the one-line fix.
W6
What is the type of formData.get('email'), and how do you get a string from it without as? (1)
FormDataEntryValue | null (a string, a File, or null when there is no such field). Narrow it: typeof value === 'string' ? value : ''.
Marking: The point needs the narrowing.
W7
A card has className={${styles.card} ${styles.cardd}} (a typo). What does npx tsc -b say, and what does the browser's Elements panel show? (1)
Nothing: every key of a CSS Module is typed string | undefined, so the typo compiles. The class attribute shows the real card class followed by the word undefined, a class that matches no rule.
Marking: The point needs both: no error, and undefined in the class.
W8
<div onClick={toggle}>Show details</div> works with a mouse. Name two things <button type="button"> gives you that the div does not. (1)
Any two of: it can be reached with Tab; Enter and Space press it; screen readers announce it as a button with its name; it shows the focus ring; jsx-a11y stops warning.
Marking: Half a point each, rounded down.
